Name: Cascara
Desc:
Cascara stands as a testament to the principles of the circular economy movement, transforming coffee fruit peels, typically discarded, into a valuable product. This innovative approach involves processing the overlooked byproduct into a brew reminiscent of fruity loose leaf tea or incorporating it into artisanal baking. 
 The introduction of single origin cascara serves a dual purpose. Primarily, it aims to create a continuous cycle of value for our producer partners at the source. Secondly, it seeks to highlight the rich sensory diversity of microlot Cascara, an often overlooked byproduct of the coffee industry. This mirrors the existing appreciation for the varied profiles found in coffee itself, presenting a new dimension to the overall coffee experience.

Name: Cross Roast Series - Drop 1
Desc:
Cross Roast Series — Siolim × One Half  
 The Cross Roast Series is a collaborative roasting project between  Siolim Specialty Coffee Roasters (India)  and  One Half Roastery (Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia).  
 For this release, each roastery roasted a coffee sourced by the other, exchanging not just green coffee, but also roasting philosophies. 
 Siolim selected one of its coffees from the Inner Pearl Series, which was roasted by  Keith Koay , four-time Malaysian Barista Champion and founder of  One Half Roastery , an award-winning roastery based in Kuala Lumpur. 
 In return, Siolim roasted one of One Half’s sourced coffees, a  Panama Geisha  from the  Cordillera region , processed as washed, a competition-level lot known for its elegance and complexity. 
 Both coffees are competition lots, showcasing how different roasting perspectives can interpret exceptional coffees. 
 The set includes two 100g coffees, presented together to allow brewers to experience this cross-roasting experiment side by side. 
 To preserve peak flavour, the coffee roasted by Keith at One Half was frozen just before its optimal resting window, ensuring the cup profile remains as expressive as intended when brewed. 
 The Cross Roast Series celebrates collaboration, craft, and the idea that roasting is interpretation even when the coffees themselves are extraordinary.

Name: Excelsa
Tasting_Notes: sweet cherry and lychee
Desc:
Excelsa — Mooleh Manay Estate, Coorg  
  Origin  
 Grown amidst the serene backwaters of the Harangi Reservoir in Coorg, Mooleh Manay Estate is a fourth- generation farm now led by Komal and Akshay Dashrath. With 75 acres of clay-loamy soil and 65 inches of annual rainfall, their approach blends data-driven precision with a deep respect for nature. Every cherry is selectively hand-picked, fermented with intent, and dried with patience each step reflecting the care and curiosity that define their craft. 
  About the Producer  
 The estate works closely with the South India Coffee Company (SICC)  a green coffee collective committed to transparency, traceability, and research. Through SICC Labs, the company explores low- intervention species and climate-resilient coffee farming, charting a sustainable future for Indian coffee. 
  Why Excelsa  
 While most of the world’s attention rests on Arabica and Robusta, Excelsa remains a quiet outlier. A rare coffee species that bridges intensity and intrigue. Once grown along farm borders in India, Excelsa trees tower high and challenge harvesters with their wild nature. Yet within their small, round beans lies an extraordinary spectrum of flavor — bright, juicy, and surprisingly complex. 
 The Mooleh Manay Excelsa lot we roast has been DNA-verified by the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew, and naturally carries a low caffeine content (0.9–0.98%) without compromising on depth. Even in milk-based brews, it retains its vivid fruit character, a rarity in the world of coffee. 
  Processing  
 This lot underwent an 84-hour yeast-inoculated natural fermentation, sealed in oxygen-restricted tanks to create a carbonic maceration environment. 
 - Harvesting: Only fully ripe cherries - hand-picked one by one. 
 - Sorting: Water flotation ensures uniform density and ripeness. 
 - Fermentation: Controlled yeast fermentation deepens sweetness and clarity. 
 - Drying: Slow, steady drying on raised beds within polyhouses. 
 - Resting: After reaching 11–12% moisture, the coffee rests for two months to allow its flavors to mature naturally. 
  Cup Profile  
 A cup that bursts with layered berry complexity, rounded by notes of sweet cherry and lychee. Low in caffeine, yet high in character - Excelsa is a reminder that beauty often thrives in the margins. 
  At Siolim  
 We roast this coffee to celebrate its unconventional story, a species often overlooked, rediscovered with care. Excelsa challenges our understanding of what Indian coffee can be: wild, bold, and beautifully untamed.

Name: Pulse
Desc: This coffee undergoes a meticulously controlled anaerobic fermentation in bio-fermenters for 42 hours, using lab-isolated microbial cultures to guide flavor development with precision. Prior to drying, the coffee is subjected to a thermal shock treatment, locking in aromatic complexity and enhancing structure. It is then slow-dried on raised beds for 23 days, following a natural processing approach that preserves clarity while building depth and sweetness.

Name: Ratnagiri Estate Washed Coffee
Tasting_Notes: dark chocolate, cherry fruit, and raisins, making it a clean and vibrant cup grown at 1350 MASL
Desc: Ratnagiri Washed coffee undergoes a meticulous washed process, where the ripe Cauvery cherries are carefully picked and pulped to remove the outer fruit. The beans are then fermented to break down any remaining mucilage, followed by a thorough washing with fresh water. This process highlights the coffee's intrinsic flavors, bringing out the rich notes of dark chocolate, cherry fruit, and raisins, making it a clean and vibrant cup grown at 1350 MASL

Name: Raxidi Lobo's P1 Natural
Desc: The finest coffee cherries were selectively picked, then thoroughly washed and placed in a stainless steel container. A P1 strain, a mix of yeast and bacteria, was then introduced to ferment the cherries in an anaerobic environment for 18 hours. Once fermentation was complete, the cherries were transferred to raised beds for slow drying over 21 days. Throughout the drying process, the temperature and humidity were carefully monitored to maintain a controlled environment.
